title: examples: RAG playground with tool-calling recipes and docs
author: Marina Soto
description: Motivation: Provide a compact, self-contained RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) playground that showcases (1) how to wire Redwood API embeddings + vector store, (2) a simple retriever + scaffolded prompt templates, and (3) safe tool-calling recipes (web search and a sandboxed python REPL) for agent workflows. This PR adds a runnable example (Docker + local node/ts dev server), step-by-step docs, and a short tutorial in the examples index. The goal is to give engineers a fast path to explore RAG workflows and tool-calling behavior without needing production infra. What this includes: examples/rag-playground/README.md with quickstart and architecture diagram; examples/rag-playground/docker-compose.yaml to bootstrap a local vector DB (Chroma) and the example app; examples/rag-playground/app/ contains a minimal TypeScript express server that demonstrates: embedding ingestion, a retriever that uses cosine similarity, a cache-aware retrieval policy, and an agent that uses Redwood's function/tool calling to invoke a web-search wrapper and a sandboxed Python REPL tool. The docs include usage patterns, security notes (sandboxing the REPL, rate limits on web search), and a troubleshooting section. Checklist: - [x] runnable locally via docker-compose - [x] minimal dataset + ingest script - [x] short tutorial in examples index - [x] function-calling examples and tests - [x] docs site entry and crosslink to Redwood API reference. Backwards compatibility: none of the changes touch platform runtime code; these are examples and docs only. Next steps: add a parity Python example and a Jupyter notebook for internal empoyee demos. Links: Linear ENG-7123 for the playground epic.

release_notes: Add: RAG playground example showcasing embeddings + retriever + tool-calling recipes (web-search and sandboxed python REPL) and documentation. Good starter for engineers exploring RAG patterns.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps runtime interactions mocked for the web-search tool; production integrations should replace mock with authenticated connector. The Python REPL is sandboxed but still only for demo purposes. Follow up PR will add a Python reference implementation and a small dataset ingestion example for FAQ demos.
